- For an individual investor, the practical Claude stack is: equity-research + financial-analysis plugins (skills work without paid connectors if you supply filings) + one cheap data MCP (Financial Datasets/Alpha Vantage/Yahoo for US; Kite MCP/Trendlyne for India) + saved red-team prompts.
- Institutional connectors (FactSet, S&P, Morningstar) are the main moat of "Claude for Financial Services"; retail users will mostly lack them.

`case_study:paytm-ipo-2021` | 2021-11-18 | tickers: PAYTM | confidence: verified

One 97 Communications (Paytm) raised Rs 18,300 cr at Rs 2,150/share in Nov 2021 (then India's largest IPO; ~Rs 10,000 cr was offer-for-sale by existing holders). It listed at Rs 1,950 on 18 Nov 2021 and closed at Rs 1,564 (-27%), the worst mainboard debut by size. By Nov 2022 it was ~79% below issue (~Rs 440s). In Mar 2022 RBI barred Paytm Payments Bank (an associate) from onboarding customers; on 31 Jan 2024 RBI ordered PPBL to stop most deposit/credit business from Feb-Mar 2024 citing 'persistent non-compliances', and the stock hit back-to-back 20% lower circuits to ~Rs 300-440 range (exact low unverified). It later recovered substantially as losses narrowed (2024-25). Visible flags at IPO: (1) loss-making since inception with no clear path to profit; (2) valuation ~50x sales-ish on a payments business with near-zero UPI margins; (3) big OFS = insiders selling; (4) QIB book subscribed only ~2.8x; (5) Macquarie's pre-listing Rs 1,200 target (-44%); (6) regulatory dependence on a related payments bank. Lesson: IPOs where insiders sell most of the issue at peak private valuations have poor base rates; regulator actions on a related entity are a key risk. Not a fraud -- a valuation and regulatory blowup, partly reversed.

**Lesson:** Avoid IPOs priced at last private round with heavy OFS; check regulatory dependence
**Spotted early by:** Macquarie (Suresh Ganapathy)

`case_study:eicher-motors` · tickers: EICHERMOT · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted (2020 1:10 split) ₹16.65 (Oct 2008) → ₹3,262 (Sep 2017) ≈196x. Twin engine: P/E 12.8 → 50.7 (4x) × implied EPS ~49x. Max drawdown inside the run only −26% (2010–11); −69% in 2008 before it. Early signals: in 2004–05 Siddhartha Lal (CEO) sold 13 of 15 group businesses to focus on Royal Enfield and trucks (Volvo JV 2008), a focus move most investors ignored. Classic 350 launched 2009; RE volumes grew ~22% CAGR 2010–18; waiting periods and dealer feedback were visible scuttlebutt. A small, fast segment (RE) sat inside a 'truck company' (hidden-segment pattern). From FY15, after Volvo-JV accounting changed, OPM was 27–31% and ROCE ~50%. Ended: volumes peaked FY19 and EPS fell from ~₹77 to ~₹40 (2020); the stock fell −61% to ₹1,268 (Apr 2020). Recovery: ₹8,058 on 19 Nov 2026 (ATH), EPS 3.4x since 2017 while P/E fell 51 → 37, so a 2017-peak buyer made 2.5x in 9 years. Lesson: focus plus a cult product plus operating leverage gives a twin-engine; when unit growth stops, even a great franchise halves. Correction to earlier record: the '86x from ₹32 (2005)' figure understates the 2008–17 run.

Key data: **start_year**: 2008; **end_year**: 2017; **start_price**: 16.65; **end_price**: 3262; **price_nov2026**: 8058; **multiple**: ~196x (2008-17); ~484x to Nov 2026; **pe_start**: 12.8; **pe_end**: 50.7; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~49x; **max_drawdown**: -26% in run; -61% 2017-20; **early_signals**: 2004-05 divest 13 of 15 businesses; Classic 350 (2009); waiting lists; RE segment inside truck company; **ended**: volume peak FY19; **lesson**: focus + operating leverage; volume stall halves even great franchises

`person:group-lanco` · flag: **poor** · confidence: single-source · tickers: LITL

Flag: POOR (leverage-driven wipe-out; no regulator fraud finding located). Hyderabad power-EPC group whose Lanco Infratech was among RBI's first 12 IBC referrals (2017) with group debt reported ~Rs 40,000 cr+; after creditors rejected Thriveni Earthmovers' revised bid, NCLT Hyderabad ordered liquidation (27-Aug-2018) -- equity effectively zero; IBBI records show liquidation still in process with a May-2026 stakeholder list. Lenders also pursued promoter Madhusudhan Rao as personal guarantor (NCLT personal-guarantee insolvency matter, 2021). Governance pattern: listed holdco funded multiple SPVs (Amarkantak, Udupi -- sold to Adani 2015, Teesta, Babandh, Vidarbha) and an Australian coal acquisition (Griffin, 2011) with corporate guarantees; EPC revenue booked from own group SPVs (related-party revenue inflating the holdco P&L); multiple CDR rounds (2013-2014) before IBC. A Business Standard analysis used Lanco to illustrate how a failed group-level resolution destroys value when each SPV is resolved separately. No CBI/SEBI fraud finding against the promoter was found in this scan -- do not describe it as fraud. Lesson: EPC 'order book' from captive SPVs is not third-party revenue; group guarantees convert one project's failure into holdco failure.

- **red flags:** related-party EPC revenue; group guarantees; CDR then IBC

`insight:buffett-japan-trading-houses-buybacks` | confidence: verified | date: 2025-02-22

2024 letter: Berkshire began buying ITOCHU, Marubeni, Mitsubishi, Mitsui and Sumitomo in July 2019: 'We simply looked at their financial records and were amazed at the low prices of their stocks.' What they liked: the five 'increase dividends when appropriate, they repurchase their shares when it is sensible to do so, and their top managers are far less aggressive in their compensation programs than their U.S. counterparts.' Initial cap below 10% of each, relaxed moderately; aggregate cost $13.8bn at end-2024 (market value $23.5bn per the letter); position partly funded with yen borrowings to match currency. 2023 letter on buybacks: 'All stock repurchases should be price-dependent. What is sensible at a discount to business-value becomes stupid if done at a premium.' And on Coke/AmEx (held 20+ years with no trades in 2023): 'When you find a truly wonderful business, stick with it. Patience pays, and one wonderful business can offset the many mediocre decisions that are inevitable.' Also 2023: 'By both luck and pluck, a few huge winners have emerged from a great many dozens of decisions.' Actionable: (1) plain-vanilla reading of financials in an unfashionable market can be an edge (cf. Indian PSUs 2020-21, Japan 2019); (2) judge Indian buybacks on price vs intrinsic value, not as a signal per se; (3) a few winners drive lifetime returns - don't trim them for 'valuation' alone.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2024ltr.pdf
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2023ltr.pdf

- Compare the effective tax rate with the statutory rate: 25.17% under India's new regime (s.115BAA, from FY20), 21% US federal plus state.
- **Causes:**
  - DTA recognition or reversal (Suzlon, Lesson 4.3)
  - tax-exempt gains (HUL FY26)
  - regime switch (FY20 one-time DTA remeasurement across India Inc.)
  - SEZ or holiday expiry
  - uncertain tax positions
- **Rule:** value on PBT × normalised rate. Treat any year with ETR below 15% or above 35% as non-representative unless it is structural.
